topic: When the DeepSeek API goes down, your local GGUF keeps generating
title: DeepSeek outage: your GGUF has no status page
description: working description; the package stage overwrites
hook_candidates: DeepSeek went down last night. Yours didn't have to.
DeepSeek gives away the model and sells the uptime.
Four hours fifty-two minutes dark. Your copy didn't notice.
Your model isn't down. Its website is.
Cloud API or local file? One outage decides.
A four-hundred-gigabyte file that never goes down.
The API went down. The model didn't go anywhere.
You pay for uptime, not intelligence.
Five incidents in October. Your disk had zero.
When DeepSeek blinks out, your GPU doesn't care.
narration_full: DeepSeek went down last night. Yours didn't have to. You just watched its status page log four hours and fifty-two minutes of downtime. You chat with DeepSeek in the browser, or you call its API from your side projects. Either way, it feels like one thing. Somewhere along the way, the website became the model. DeepSeek is two things stacked. The model is files of numbers, called its parameters. The service is someone else's computers running those files for you. Last night, that service went dark. The files did not change. One of those two things can live on your disk. Treat the chat app like a streaming service. The GGUF file, a single file holding a whole model, is the disc on your shelf. The service going dark does not touch the disc. DeepSeek published the R one weights, the trained model files themselves, free for anyone under the MIT license. They sit on Hugging Face right now. LM Studio or llama.cpp runs the file on your machine. No account, no API key, no status page to check. Now the honest part. At the common download quality, the full DeepSeek R one is a four hundred four gigabyte file. Your gaming PC is not loading that. Neither is your Mac. DeepSeek also shipped distills, smaller models trained to imitate the big one. One of those carries seven billion parameters. Unsloth's GGUF card sizes it against a twenty-four gigabyte gaming GPU, an RTX forty ninety for example. One catch. A disc holds the identical movie. Your copy is cut down, so the quality genuinely drops. When you need the full model's best answers, the cloud is still where that brain lives. The API was never the model. A file on your disk has no status page.
